data.name: Kliment
data.gender_notes: Kliment is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'klēmēn', meaning 'mild' or 'gentle'. In Christian tradition, Saint Clement of Rome is the third pope and a key figure in early Christianity. The name Kliment carries the meaning “Mild, gentle” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Kliment usually hope their child will grow to embody mild, gentle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Kliment belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mild, gentle.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kliment total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_greek.name: Κλιμἐντ
in_greek.meaning: βασιλεύς εἰρήνης, πηγή εἰρήνης, εἰρήνη του σαῦλον
in_greek.long_meaning: ὁ ὄνομα Κλιμἐντ ἔχει τὴν ἱστορίαν τοῦ σαῦλον ἀπὸ τὴν ἑβραϊκή γλώσσα, τὸ ὀνύματι ἐξαρχόμενον ἀπὸ τῆς ἑβραϊκῆς λέξεως עלחלנניעיל. Ἡ λέξη Κλιμἐντ ἐμφανίζεται σὲ τὴν Βίβλο σὲ τὴν Πράξη τῶν Ἀποστόλων (Ἀπ. 11:30) καὶ ὑποδηλώνει τὸν χριστιανικόν ἔρχεsten τοῦ σαῦλον. Ἐπίσης, ἡ λέξη Κλιμἐντ ἐμφανίζεται σὲ τὴν Ἐκκλησιαστική Ἀγωγή τῆς Ἀγίας Γραφῆς π. 3:11, ὅπου ὑποδηλώνει τὴν εἰρήνην τῶν χριστιανῶν.

in_latin.name: Kliment
in_latin.meaning: rex pacis, fons pacis, pacem salus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Klimentum originem habet a lingua Hebraica, unde significat pacem, fonsque pacis. In libro Actuum Apostolorum (Act. 11:30) et in Ecclesiastica Rituale Sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae, Klimentum significat pacem Christianorum.

in_english.name: Kliment
in_english.meaning: King of peace, source of peace, peace salvation
in_english.long_meaning: The name Kliment has its origin in the Hebrew language, meaning peace, source of peace. In the Acts of the Apostles (Acts 11:30) and in the Ecclesiastical Ritual of the Roman Catholic Church, Kliment is a reference to the peace of Christians. Kliment is a name derived from the Greek word 'Klimakos' (Κλίμακος), meaning ladder, which in turn refers to the spiritual journey of Christians. This name has been used in Eastern Orthodox tradition to signify the peaceful and harmonious coexistence among Christians. Kliment is also associated with the virtue of peace and tranquility, and is seen as a symbol of the unity and solidarity among believers.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kliment bears a rich cultural heritage rooted in ancient Greek language and early Christian history. Named after St. Clement of Rome, the third pope, the name represents gentleness, mildness, and wisdom, essential virtues in Christian leadership. Across cultures, without excluding Eastern Europe, the name is celebrated and cherished due to its association with one of the most influential figures of early Christianity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kliment holds spiritual significance as a reminder of Christ's gentle and loving nature. Inspired by St. Clement of Rome, the name embodies the patience, kindness, and humility that Christians are called to reflect. It also symbolizes the importance of spiritual guidance and leadership in the faith journey, as demonstrated by St. Clement's role in the early Christian community.
